parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *aika. Cognate to Finnish aika, Ingrian aika, Livvi aigu, Ludian aig, Veps aig, Votic aikõ and Livonian āiga. Possibly from or akin to Proto-Germanic *aiwaz (compare Gothic 𐌰𐌹𐍅𐍃 (aiws, “age, eternity”), Old Norse ævi (“lifetime”), English aye). Another possibility is the borrowing
From Proto-Finnic *airo, from Proto-Germanic *airō. Cognate with Finnish and Votic airo.

parole.significato: an oven (a chamber used for baking or heating)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Finnic *ahjo (“oven”), from earlier *ašjo, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *asjǭ (“soapstone”). .

parole.significato: a glade (grassy open or cleared space in a forest, especially one that is a result of slash-and-burn cultivation)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Finnic *aho (“a glade”), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *askǭ (“ash, ashes”), possibly from Proto-Indo-European *h₂e(H)s- (“to dry, burn”), from *h₂eh₁-.

From Proto-Finnic *ainaga, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *ainagaz, compare English any, Dutch enig, German einig, Icelandic einigur and Gothic 𐌰𐌹𐌽𐌰𐌷𐍃 (ainahs). Also posited to be a borrowing from Baltic, compare Latvian viens, Lithuanian vienas, Old Prussian ains. Cognates include Finnish ainoa, Voti
From Proto-Finnic *antura, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *anduraz. Cognate with Ingrian antura, Finnish antura, Old Norse ǫndurr (“snowshoe”) and Swedish andor.
From Proto-Finnic *arka, from Proto-Germanic *argaz. Compare German arg.

From Proto-Finnic *auvo, itself possibly from Proto-Germanic *auja-, compare Old Norse ey (“luck, heavenly aid”) and Gothic 𐌰𐍅𐌹- (awi-) in 𐌰𐍅𐌹𐌻𐌹𐌿𐌸 (awiliuþ). Cognate to Finnish auvo and Livonian o’v. Possibly related to the verb avama.
From Proto-Finnic *äitei, from Proto-Germanic *aiþį̄, cognate to Finnish äiti.
From Proto-Finnic *haava, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hawwa- (“blow, hit”) or early Proto-Norse *hawwa-, compare Icelandic högg (“hit, stroke”). Cognate with Finnish haava and Votic aavõ.
Derived from Proto-Finnic *haja-, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sājan-, *sēaną. Related to Finnish hajota.
From Proto-Finnic *halpa, from Proto-Germanic *salwaz. Cognates include Finnish halpa (“cheap”), more distantly English sallow.
From Proto-Finnic *heittädäk, possibly from Proto-Germanic *sēaną (“to sow”). Compare German säen (“to sow”) and Gothic 𐍃𐌰𐌹𐌰𐌽 (saian). Cognate to Finnish heittää.

From Proto-Finnic *hiici. Cognate with Finnish Finnish hiisi and Livvi hiiži (“devil”). The original meaning in Proto-Finnic was most likely "burial ground". Possibly a loan from Proto-Germanic *χīđiz (“den, thicket”) or *sīdǭ (“side”).
From Proto-Finnic *hilja, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *silāną.
From Proto-Finnic *hoora, from Proto-Germanic *hōrǭ. Possibly a newer loan from Old Swedish hōra. Cognate to Finnish huora and English whore.
From Proto-Finnic *hulkka, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *fulką.
From Proto-Finnic *ja, from Proto-Germanic *jahw (“and”); compare Gothic 𐌾𐌰𐌷 (jah), Old High German ja, joh.

parole.significato: Emphasises what is spoken, usually because it is already known and obvious to both parties.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jo (“already”), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *ju (“already; yet; now”). Cognate to Finnish jo, Votic jo, and Ludian ďo.
From Proto-Finnic *juusto, from Proto-Germanic *justaz. Related to Finnish juusto, Swedish ost.
From Proto-Finnic *kaappidak, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skabaną. Compare German schaben. Cognate to Finnish kaapia.
From Proto-Finnic *kansa (“companion”), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hansō.

From Proto-Germanic *hafraz. Compare Old English hæfer (“he-goat”). Cognate to Finnish kauris. The word had only survived naturally in place-names, it was revived in the written language at the end of the 20th century.
From Proto-Finnic *kallijo, from Proto-Germanic *hallijǭ. Compare Swedish häll and Old Norse hella. Cognate to Finnish kallio.
From Proto-Finnic *kaldas, from Proto-Germanic *halþaz. Compare Old Norse hallr. Cognate to Finnish kallas.
From Proto-Finnic *kana, from Proto-Germanic *hanô. Cognates include Finnish kana.
From Proto-Finnic *karja, which is likely borrowed from Proto-Germanic *harjaz. Cognate with Finnish karja.
From Proto-Finnic *kattila, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *katilaz.
From Proto-Finnic *kaccodak, possibly from Proto-Germanic *gātijaną. Cf. Icelandic gæta (“watch over, look after”). Cognate to Finnish katsoa.

parole.significato: beautiful (pleasant in appearance, satisfying to look at)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaunis, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skauniz.
From Proto-Finnic *kauppa, from Proto-Germanic *kaupaz, compare German Kauf and Old Norse kaup. Cognate to Finnish kauppa, Votic kauppõ, Ingrian kauppa, Livvi kauppu, and Ludian kaup.
From Proto-Finnic *kellä, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skellǭ (“bell”).
From Proto-Finnic *kiireh. Cognate to Finnish kiire and Votic čiire. Possibly the same root as in dialectal Estonian and Finnish kiiras; from Proto-Germanic *gīraz, compare Old High German giri.
From Proto-Finnic *kilpi, possibly from Proto-Germanic *hlībō. Compare Old Norse hlíf. Possibly from Proto-Germanic *skelbi-, *skilbi-. Compare the Old Norse royal family name Skilfingar.

parole.significato: zander, the freshwater fish Sander lucioperca.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kuha, borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?].
From Proto-Finnic *kotti, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *kuddô. Compare English cod. Cognate to Votic kotti and dialectal Finnish kotti.
From Proto-Finnic *kukkoi, from Proto-Germanic *kukkaz. Cognates include Finnish kukko.
From Proto-Finnic *kulta, from Proto-Germanic *gulþą.

parole.significato: king (the title of male head of state of a monarchist country)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kuningas, from Proto-Germanic *kuningaz.
From Proto-Finnic *kurkku, from Proto-Germanic *kwerkō. Cognates include Finnish kurkku.
From Proto-Finnic *këlbat'ak, from Proto-Germanic *helpaną, compare German helfen (“to help”). Cognate to Finnish kelvata and Votic kõlvõtõ.

parole.significato: to stack, to lay, to pile
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *latoidak, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *hlaþaną.

parole.significato: ship (a large watercraft for carrying people or goods)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *laiva, from Proto-Germanic *flawją. Cognate with Finnish laiva.
From Proto-Finnic *laita, from Proto-Germanic *laidō. Compare Old Norse leið. Cognate to Finnish laita.
Derived from Proto-Finnic *lama, from Proto-Germanic *lamaz. Compare English lame. Cognate to Finnish lama (“depression”), lamata (“to paralyse”), and Votic lamata (“to lay, to fell”).
From Proto-Finnic *lambas, from Proto-Germanic *lambaz.
Inherited from Proto-Finnic *lauta, possibly from Proto-Germanic *flauþ or *flaut. Compare Swedish flöte. Also compare Lithuanian plaũtas and Latvian plàukts.

parole.significato: allium (type of plant including onion and garlic)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *laukka, from Proto-Germanic *laukaz; compare Finnish laukka, Swedish lök, German Lauch, and English leek.
From Proto-Finnic *lautta, from Proto-Germanic *lautō, *lautiz. Compare Old Norse laut and Old Swedish lȫt. Cognate to Votic lauttõ.

From Proto-Finnic *lebäit'äk, cognate to Finnish levätä. Possibly from Proto-Germanic *hliwjaną (compare Middle High German ge-liuwen (“to rest”)) or Proto-Germanic *slēpaną (“to sleep”) (compare Old English slæpan (“to sleep”)). Originally a rarely-used dialectal word, but it was brought into the s
From Proto-Finnic *leepedä, ultimately probably from Proto-Germanic *hlēwaz. Cognate to Ingrian leepeä and Livonian līebdõ. See also Finnish lievä.
From Proto-Finnic *laipa, from Proto-Germanic *hlaibaz.
From Proto-Finnic *lupa, from Proto-Germanic *lubą (“praise”).
From Proto-Finnic *lëivo, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *laiwaz (whence *laiwazikǭ, from which English lark). Cognate to Finnish leivo.
From Proto-Finnic *mako, ultimately loaned from Proto-Germanic *magô. Cognate to Votic mako.
From Proto-Finnic *mahti, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *mahtiz. Cognate to Finnish mahti (“might, power”).

parole.significato: Someone with a liking for sweet foods, a sweet tooth.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *makjas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *smakjaz.

parole.significato: to use words in a magical way
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *manat'ak, probably from Proto-Germanic *manōną, compare German mahnen, or, less likely, from Proto-Uralic *mᴕnɜ- (“to say”). Cognate to Finnish manata and Ingrian manada.
From Proto-Finnic *markka, from Proto-Germanic *marką.

From Proto-Finnic *mees. Possibly derived from Proto-Germanic *mēgaz (earlier Proto-Finnic *meexes), compare Gothic 𐌼𐌴𐌲𐍃 (mēgs, “son-in-law”), Old English mǣġ (“relative”) and Old Norse mágr (“male relative”), although this proposal is questionable for phonetic reasons. Cognate with Finnish mies, Li
From Proto-Finnic *multa, from Proto-Germanic *muldō.
From Proto-Finnic *musta. Cognate with Finnish musta, Veps must and Livonian mustā. Possibly from Proto-Germanic *mus-ta-, compare Norwegian Bokmål must (“steam, fume, mist”).
From Proto-Finnic *mët'ëldak, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *metaną, compare Dutch meten. Cognate to Votic mõtõllõ and Livonian mõtlõ.

From Proto-Finnic *mëëkka, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *mēkijaz (compare Old Norse mækir, Norwegian Nynorsk mækje (“iris”) and Gothic 𐌼𐌴𐌺𐌴𐌹𐍃 (mēkeis)). Cognates include Finnish miekka, Livonian mȭk, Votic mõõkkõ, Ingrian meekka, Karelian miekka and Ludian miek.
From Proto-Finnic *mëëtto, from Proto-Germanic *mētō. Cognate with Votic mõõtto, mõõttu.
From Proto-Finnic *nakla, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *naglaz. The meaning of "unit of mass" was possibly influenced by German Nagel.
From Proto-Finnic *nootta, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *nōtō.
From Proto-Finnic *ohja, cognate to Finnish ohja and Votic õhjõ. Possibly a loan from Proto-Germanic *ansijō.
From Proto-Finnic *patja, from Proto-Germanic *badją. Related to Finnish patja.
From Proto-Finnic *paikka, from Proto-Germanic *spaikō. Cognate with Finnish paikka and Votic paikkõ.
From Proto-Finnic *pakko. Cognate to Finnish pakko (“stump, block of rotten wood”). Possibly from Proto-Germanic *spaikǭ. Compare Dutch spaak (“broom, spoke”).

parole.significato: it's all good, all right (a saying expressing moderate satisfaction or said as a consolation)
parole.testo: First part pole (“is not; are not”), a contraction of older ep ole (Modern Estonian: ei ole (“is not, are not”). Second part viga (“mistake, fault”), from Proto-Finnic *vika (“fault, defect, mistake”), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *swiką (“deceit; deception; trickery”), from Proto-Indo-Euro

parole.significato: sail (a vertical surface made of fabric or the like, which, when attached to the mast, catches the wind and makes the s…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *purjëh, from Proto-Germanic *buriz. Cognate with Finnish purje and Votic purjõ.

parole.significato: field (arable, cultivated land used mainly for growing short rotation crops)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pëlto, from Proto-Germanic *felþuz (compare Old English feld, English field, German Feld, Swedish fjäll (“mountain”)). Cognates include Finnish pelto, Votic põlto, Ingrian peldo, Karelian pelto, Livvi peldo, Ludian peld and Veps pöud.

parole.significato: instep (top of the foot between the toes and the ankle)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Finnic *peütä, from Proto-Germanic *beudaz. Finnish pöytä.
From Proto-Finnic *rata, from Proto-Germanic *tradō (“track, way”). Compare Low German trade (“track, rut”).
From Proto-Finnic *rahvas, from Proto-Germanic *þrawwaz (“full-grown”).
From Proto-Finnic *rakjoidak, possibly from Proto-Germanic *rakjaną. Cognate with dialectal Finnish raajoa.
From Proto-Finnic *raukka, possibly from Proto-Germanic *draugaz, whence also Old Norse draugr.
From Proto-Finnic *riita, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *strīdaz Related to Finnish riita.
From Proto-Finnic *rik'as, from Proto-Germanic *rīkijaz. Cognate with German reich (“rich”).
From Proto-Finnic *rooho, from Proto-Germanic *grasą (“grass”).
From Proto-Finnic *rëngas, from Proto-Germanic *hringaz. Compare German Ring. Cognate to Finnish rengas. See also ring.

parole.significato: saddle (seat placed on the back or withers of a horse or another animal)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *satula, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sadulaz (“saddle”). Cognates include Finnish satula, Võro satol', Livonian sa’ddõl, Votic satulõ, Ingrian satula, Livvi saduli, Ludian and Veps sadul.
From Proto-Finnic *sallidak, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *saljaną, compare Swedish sälja. Cognate to Finnish sallia and Votic sallia.

Inherited from Proto-Finnic *sama (“same”), borrowed from Proto-Germanic *samaz (“same, alike”), from Proto-Indo-European *somHós (“same, alike”), presumably from *sem- (“together, one”). Cognate with Finnish sama, Norwegian Bokmål samme, Swedish samma, Danish samme, and English same.

From Proto-Finnic *sakna, possibly from Proto-Germanic *stakkaz (“a barn; rick; haystack”), cognate with English stack, Old Norse stakkr (“stack”) and dialectal Swedish stake (“hearth, fireplace”). Possibly also from Proto-Germanic *sāpnaz (“a place of soap”). Cognate with Finnish sauna, Livvi saunu

parole.significato: sieve (device to separate larger objects from smaller ones or from liquids)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sëkla, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *sēdlą. Cognate with Finnish seula and Ingrian seegla.
From Proto-Finnic *tarbis, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *þarbaz, *þarbō. Compare Swedish tarv and Gothic 𐌸𐌰𐍂𐌱𐌰 (þarba). Cognate to Finnish tarve and Votic tarviz.
From Proto-Finnic *tuppi, possibly from Proto-Germanic *duppa, compare German Topf (“pot”). Cognate to Finnish tuppi.

parole.significato: cod (any marine fish of the family Gadidae)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Finnic *turska, from Proto-Germanic *þurskaz, from Proto-Indo-European *ters- + *-ḱos. Compare Finnish turska.

From Proto-Finnic *turva, possibly from Proto-Germanic *trūwɔ̄n. Compare Old Norse trúa (“belief”). Cognate to Finnish turva and Votic turva (Rudja). The word was brought into the standard language in example of Finnish.

parole.significato: peat, turf (Soil formed of dead but not fully decayed plants found in bog areas)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *turbas, from Proto-Germanic *turbz. Compare German Torf. Cognate to Finnish turve, Votic turvaz (Kattila), and Veps turbaz.

From Proto-Finnic *topi, from Proto-Germanic *dawīni-, *dawēn-, or *dawa-. Compare Old Norse dán (“death”), Icelandic sví-dái (“dead (of natural causes, for farm animals)”), and Old Norse dá (“unconsciousness, hibernation”), respectively. Cognate to Livonian te’b, tö’b.
From Proto-Finnic *umpi, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *umbi (“around, about, by, near”). Cognate with Finnish umpi-.

parole.significato: to believe, to have faith in something
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *uskodak, from Proto-Germanic *wunskijaną, cf. Old Norse œskja. Cognate with Finnish uskoa.
From Proto-Finnic *vaha, from Proto-Germanic *wahsą or Proto-Baltic *waksa, *vakša. Compare English wax and Latvian vasks, respectively.

parole.significato: carpet, rug; tapestry (textile covering a surface)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vaippa, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *waipaz (compare Old Norse veipa, veipr (“headscarf, kerchief”) and Gothic 𐍅𐌰𐌹𐍀𐍃 (waips, “crown, wreath”)). Cognate with Votic vaippa (“carpet”) and Finnish vaippa (“diaper; mantle, cloak, robe”).
From Proto-Finnic *valta, from Proto-Germanic *waldą. Cognate to Finnish valta and Swedish våld.

parole.significato: to choose, to pick, to select
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *validak, from Proto-Germanic *waljaną. Compare German wählen. Cognate to Finnish valita.
From Proto-Finnic *valo, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *kwalō. Compare Swedish kval (“agony”) and German Qual (“agony”). Possibly a derivation of valge.

From Proto-Finnic *vapras, further origin unclear, possibly from Proto-Germanic *fagraz (“fair, beautiful; proper, suitable”), thence Old Norse fagr, Old Swedish fagher and Gothic 𐍆𐌰𐌲𐍂𐍃 (fagrs). Compare Finnish vauras and Karelian vauras.

parole.significato: property, estate, goods; things belonging to a person or organisation
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Finnic *vara, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *warō, compare Swedish vara, German Ware, English ware. Cognate to Finnish vara and Livonian varā.
From Proto-Finnic *vargas, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wargaz.
From Proto-Finnic *varëh, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *waruz.
From Proto-Finnic *venät, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *weneđ- (“Slav”) or Proto-Germanic *winidaz (“Slav”). Cognates include Estonian venelane, and Finnish venäläinen, venakko, venäjä and Venäjä.

parole.significato: mistake, error, fault (failure to comply with a rule, norm, standard, fact, etc., deviation from correct performance)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vika, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *swiką (“deception”). Cognates include Votic, Ingrian, and Finnish vika (“ailment, disease; fault, error; fault; defect; disability; disorder; bad habit”), Livonian vigā (“error; disease; fault; cause”), Karelian, Livvi, and Veps viga (“defect; e
From Proto-Finnic *vihko, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *wiskō, *wiskaz.

parole.significato: about, amount, by, much (used to indicate inexact quantities in comparison to something else)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Finnic *vërta, from Proto-Germanic *werþaz. Cognate with Finnish verta.
